entries.what_happened: One manuscript, 'Rokhlin's multiple-mixing problem for one transformation' (dated 23 September 2026; the only manuscript in this family). Its main theorem (introduction, thm:main) says: if T is an invertible measure-preserving transformation with measurable inverse on an arbitrary probability space (no standardness or countable-generation assumption) and T is mixing, meaning mu(A cap T^{-n}B) -> mu(A)mu(B) as |n| -> infinity, then for every k >= 3 and all measurable A_1,...,A_k, mu(A_1 cap T^{-n_1}A_2 cap ... cap T^{-(n_1+...+n_{k-1})}A_k) -> product of mu(A_i) as min(n_1,...,n_{k-1}) -> infinity through positive integers. The manuscript counts order by the number of sets (order k = k sets, which it says is multiplicity k-1 in Rokhlin's and Ryzhikov's convention). The proof is by contradiction on a least failing order k. Section 2 extracts a zero-entropy mixing finite-alphabet shift with centred one-site functions that witness a nonvanishing k-fold correlation along diverging layouts. Sections 3-6 build a saturated ordered array object, an operator description of exact lines, measurable labels grouped into finite blocks, and a one-dimensional cancellation result (Proposition orbit-cancellation) that makes the Cesaro averages of the block coefficients vanish. Section 7 integrates these to contradict a constant positive block integral. Section 8 (Corollary, endomorphisms and flows) extends the conclusion to (1) non-invertible measurable endomorphisms on arbitrary probability spaces, for forward times only, and (2) real-time flows whose Koopman operators are strongly continuous on L^1.
entries.delivers: Answers the bullet's question affirmatively for a single invertible measure-preserving transformation (a Z-action, the classical setting) on any probability space: every strongly (2-fold) mixing system is strongly 3-mixing, and in fact mixing of every order k >= 3. Order 3 in the manuscript is three sets, which matches the bullet's A_0, A_1, A_2 reading; the all-k statement also covers the four-set (A_0,...,A_3) reading. Restrictions: (a) convergence is along layouts whose successive gaps tend to infinity, i.e. min(n_1, n_2) -> infinity for three sets with n_1 = t_2 - t_1 and n_2 = t_3 - t_2, with t_1 = 0 by invariance. This is the gap form the introduction uses to define mixing of order k. The manuscript does not state a condition that each shift diverges separately, so the bullet's phrase 'shifts m_1, m_2 -> infinity' is ambiguous here and the manuscript's statement is the gap form. (b) The hypothesis is two-sided mixing, which for invertible T is the bullet's strong mixing. (c) The manuscript says Theorem thm:main 'answers Rokhlin's multiple-mixing problem affirmatively for one transformation', and its abstract says the same. Its framing (whether ordinary mixing alone implies the next order) matches the bullet in substance. The endomorphism and flow corollaries go beyond the bullet: they cover non-invertible maps, and flows (R-actions) only under an extra L^1 strong-continuity hypothesis.
entries.remains: If the claim is correct, nothing remains of the bullet's question for single invertible transformations. Outside it: (i) multi-generator actions (Z^d or other groups). The introduction says the one-generator distinction is essential and cites Ledrappier's zero-entropy mixing Z^2 example, which is not threefold mixing. (ii) For flows, the continuity hypothesis is assumed, not proved, and the text treats it as automatic only for jointly measurable flows on standard probability spaces (cited). (iii) For endomorphisms, only forward times are covered.
entries.direction: proves the conjecture (affirmative: mixing implies mixing of every order k >= 3 for one invertible transformation)
entries.conditional_on: None for the main theorem beyond its stated hypotheses (invertible, measure-preserving, mixing). The proof uses standard background results (conditional-expectation convergence, the entropy chain rule, the spectral theorem for compact positive operators) and refers outward at a few steps. The saturation construction in Section 3 follows the 'method of sated extensions' of Austin, cited to a preprint version (its proof of Theorem 3.11 and Lemma 3.12) and not reproduced in full. The exponential-moment estimate for dissociated characters is cited to Green (2002, Section 2.2, Proposition 17), and the manuscript gives the projective-character version itself. The endomorphism corollary uses the natural extension of a standard factor (Rokhlin 1960, Section 9). The flow corollary assumes strong continuity of the Koopman operators on L^1; the text says this holds for jointly measurable flows on standard spaces, citing Rokhlin 1960, Section 1.7. No other manuscript in this family is used.
entries.doubts: The text flags no step as sketched or conjectural, and the main claim is not hedged. Points a reader should check: (1) Several steps are closed by 'the same argument', 'similarly', or 'the analogous assertion holds with rows and columns exchanged' (for example the common-exact-lines proposition and the incident-operator claim in Section 4, and the first-factor replacement in Section 2), so part of the verification is left to the reader. (2) The proof of Proposition orbit-cancellation (Section 6) is a short case assembly that relies on lemmas stated just before it, and the dissociated case depends on an entropy lemma whose hypothesis H_n = o(n) is checked only afterwards, via a progression-word estimate. (3) The no-standardness claim in the introduction depends on the Section 2 reduction to a finite-alphabet factor. Section 2 opens by saying it places the failure 'in a standard probability space', and the conventions say standardness is obtained only after passing to that factor. (4) The array construction is deliberately asymmetric: row independence is explicitly not asserted (Section 3), and the argument handles the other axis by permuting groups. (5) The main theorem is long (about 3,100 lines of TeX over eight sections). The abstract matches the theorem's statement.
